See the Palace of Culture and the historic Veracruz Church. Then head to Comuna 13, where vivid murals, outdoor escalators and lively streets tell the story of the neighborhood's transformation. Here the city's history comes alive through street art and everyday community life.

The final stop is El Castillo Museum. The European-style mansion houses works of art, antiques and historic furniture, and is surrounded by beautifully maintained gardens. Return to the hotel after the excursion.

The road follows the Mendoza River valley through historic Uspallata. A stop at a viewpoint is scheduled near Aconcagua.

The route runs alongside the Mendoza River, with views from the road of the Cordón del Plata range and Potrerillos Dam, built to generate electricity and distribute water for irrigation.

The next stop is Uspallata, a pre-Hispanic settlement of the Huarpe people and, according to the original itinerary, the southernmost point of the Inca Empire reached by the Inca road from Peru. Here stand the Uspallata Vaults, historic adobe structures where the chaplain Fray Luis Beltrán cast cannons and weapons.

The journey continues through Picheuta, Polvaredas and Punta de Vacas to the Los Penitentes ski resort. There is free time here, and you can take a chairlift for views of the mountains from above.

The tour then heads to Puente del Inca, a natural stone bridge with hot springs. At an altitude of 2,750 meters is the Cerro Aconcagua viewpoint, overlooking Aconcagua, which rises to 6,959 meters. From here you can also head toward Horcones Lagoon and the provincial park.

This walking tour of Mérida introduces its colonial architecture and Maya heritage. In the historic center, you will see San Ildefonso Cathedral, Plaza Zócalo and the facades of old buildings.

The route then follows Paseo de Montejo, a boulevard lined with mansions whose architecture reveals European influences. Your certified bilingual guide will explain the city's history and recommend restaurants where you can discover local cuisine.

Duration: 6 hours

• Start: 8:40–9:30 a.m.

• Language: English and Spanish

Today you will journey through the beating heart of Mexico City, where Aztec traditions meet colonial grandeur and vibrant modern life. Begin in the historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Stroll across the magnificent Zócalo, with its imposing Metropolitan Cathedral and the ruins of Templo Mayor, once the ceremonial center of ancient Tenochtitlan. Continue past the elegant Palace of Fine Arts and lively Alameda Central, where art and everyday life mingle. Later, visit the world-famous National Museum of Anthropology (closed on Mondays), a cultural treasure trove showcasing Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilizations. Admire the Aztec Sun Stone, colossal Olmec heads and richly detailed artifacts that tell the story of Mexico's indigenous roots. Your certified guide brings it all to life with insight and enthusiasm. After the tour, return to the hotel or enjoy lunch and immerse yourself in the rhythm of the capital.

Tour highlights:

● Walk through Mexico City's historic center and the ruins of ancient Tenochtitlan. Visit the monumental Metropolitan Cathedral and the magnificent Palace of Fine Arts.

● Explore the National Museum of Anthropology, home to iconic artifacts such as the Aztec Sun Stone.

● Enjoy a balance of guided exploration and free time. Round-trip transportation is included.

Included: Shared transportation, certified bilingual guide, admission to the National Museum of Anthropology, city sightseeing tour

Not included: Meals, drinks, tips, personal expenses
